title.value: When Do Graph Neural Networks Help with Node Classification? Investigating the Impact of Homophily Principle on Node Distinguishability
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus of the study on understanding when GNNs are effective for node classification with respect to the homophily principle.
title.quote: When Do Graph Neural Networks Help with Node Classification? Investigating the Impact of Homophily Principle on Node Distinguishability

extractions.description: This paper investigates the effectiveness of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in node classification tasks, specifically examining how intra-class and inter-class node distinguishability (ND) and the homophily principle affect GNN performance. It introduces a novel graph model, CSBM-H, to study these effects and proposes new metrics for node distinguishability. The study seeks to provide a better understanding of when GNNs outperform other models and introduces a classifier-based performance metric to evaluate GNN effectiveness without training.
